question.text: By 27 November 2026, how many of the two Bundibugyo-specific vaccine candidates (ChAdOx1 BDBV, mRNA-1469) will have been publicly reported as administered to Tumaini trial participants?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to the number (0, 1 or 2) of the two Bundibugyo-specific vaccine candidates for which a source published on or before 27 November 2026, 23:59 UTC reports that at least one dose had been administered to a participant of the Tumaini ring-vaccination trial in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (ClinicalTrials.gov [NCT07842107](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07842107)). The two candidates counted are ChAdOx1 BDBV (University of Oxford with the Serum Institute of India) and mRNA-1469 (Moderna); a candidate counts as soon as any such source reports a single dose given to any Tumaini participant, regardless of what is later reported about that participant's immune response or completion of the regimen, and the report need not state the exact dosing date. Ervebo (rVSV-ZEBOV, a Zaire ebolavirus vaccine) does not count, and neither do doses of the two candidates given in any other study, including the PARTNERS and EBO-PEP trials in the DRC. Resolution is based primarily on WHO statements (news releases and Disease Outbreak News), announcements by the trial sponsors and vaccine developers (INRB, Epicentre/MSF, University of Oxford, Serum Institute of India, Moderna, CEPI) and DRC Ministry of Health statements, and secondarily on the investigational-vaccine tracker at [https://ebolaintel.com/vaccines/investigational](https://ebolaintel.com/vaccines/investigational) or [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions).
question.fine_print: A candidate counts only where the source explicitly links the dose to the Tumaini trial (or to NCT07842107); reports of Bundibugyo-specific vaccination in the DRC that do not identify the trial are not sufficient. Only the two named candidates are counted — if a further Bundibugyo-specific candidate is added to Tumaini before the cutoff, it is not counted here. A candidate still counts if its arm is subsequently paused, suspended or closed after at least one dose has been given.

research:
As of 16 November 2026, no source reports a dose of either ChAdOx1 BDBV or mRNA-1469 given to a Tumaini participant, so the count is currently 0. Both candidates still need DRC national approval. WHO's Meg Doherty said around 4-5 November that dosing could begin "within three to four weeks". That points to roughly 25 November to 2 December, right around the 27 November cutoff.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-12: The ebolaintel.com tracker ("Last updated 2026-11-12") lists both ChAdOx1 BDBV and mRNA-1469 as Phase 1. It says WHO advisers recommended adding them to Tumaini "once national approvals are in place". Its only Tumaini dosing entry is Ervebo: first participants in Bunia on 23 October. It shows no Tumaini dose of either candidate. [ebolaintel](https://ebolaintel.com/vaccines/investigational)
- 2026-11-04: The WHO news release says the two candidates will join "following national approvals". It gives no start date. [WHO](https://www.who.int/news/item/04-11-2026-two-new-candidate-vaccines-to-join-ebola-trial-as-treatment-research-advances)
- I found no WHO Disease Outbreak News, sponsor statement or DRC Ministry of Health statement reporting a Tumaini dose of either candidate.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. Reported value as of 16 November: 0.
- Wikipedia says the candidates are "approved for inclusion" in Tumaini. That refers to WHO's recommendation, not DRC approval, and it reports no doses. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Central_Africa_Ebola_epidemic)
- Sources disagree on Tumaini's first-dose date: 23 October (ebolaintel, Wikipedia) versus 26 October (ITG/MSF press releases, K24). This doesn't affect the question. [ITG](https://www.itg.be/en/health-stories/press-releases/tumaini-first-participant-vaccinated)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-15/16: Six-month coverage (WHO/Tedros, Africa CDC, RFI) gives more than 11,000 confirmed cases and 5,400 to 5,568 deaths. None of the articles I saw summarised mentions either candidate being given in Tumaini. [AA](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/health/3-000-recover-from-ebola-in-dr-congo-who/4125898), [Outlook India](https://www.outlookindia.com/international/ebola-outbreak-ravages-congo-hunger-insecurity-fear-hamper-response)
- 2026-11-13: The TWiV podcast discussed Moderna's press release on mRNA-1469 "entering" the Phase 2/3 study. It reports no dosing.
- 2026-11-14: K24 says neither candidate is approved and both can enter only after national approvals. WHO told the developers on 2 November. Four rings had been set up. [K24](https://k24.digital/lifestyle/health-and-fitness/kenya-to-launch-ksh4-7-billion-ebola-vaccine-trial-in-2027-as-drc-expands-tumaini-study)
- 2026-11-10: Gavi says both still need national approval and results are expected in early 2027. It gives no start date or shipment information. [Gavi](https://www.gavi.org/vaccineswork/can-two-new-vaccines-help-turn-tide-against-ebola-caused-bundibugyo-virus)
- ~2026-11-05: Health Policy Watch quotes WHO's Meg Doherty saying the trials could begin "within three to four weeks", pending DRC regulatory approval. [HPW](https://healthpolicy-watch.news/who-greenlights-two-ebola-bundibugyo-virus-vaccine-candidates-for-phase-2-3-trials/)
- 2026-11-04: Moderna's press release says mRNA-1469 will be evaluated in Tumaini "subject to regulatory approval". CEPI is funding additional trial doses (no number given). No dosing timeline. [BioSpace](https://www.biospace.com/press-releases/moderna-advances-investigational-bundibugyo-ebolavirus-vaccine-toward-phase-2-3-study)
- 2026-10-13: CEPI named both as due to join Tumaini. WHO's immunisation director said ChAdOx1 could join quickly if its early data are positive. [ebolaintel](https://ebolaintel.com/vaccines/investigational)

**Supply (from the tracker):**
- ChAdOx1 BDBV: about 620,000 doses stockpiled by the Serum Institute. It is in two Phase 1 trials, Oxford (since 24 July) and Masaka, Uganda (since 6 October), so it is further along.
- mRNA-1469: Phase 1 in Canada since 3 August. A Uganda Phase Ib was approved on 7 October, but no enrolment has been reported.

## 4. Base rates
- Timing in this outbreak suggests lags of weeks between approval and first dose:
  - Tumaini protocol to first Ervebo dose: Ervebo's first consignment arrived in Kinshasa on 21 August, and the first Tumaini dose came on 23-26 October, about two months later. [HPW](https://healthpolicy-watch.news/who-greenlights-two-ebola-bundibugyo-virus-vaccine-candidates-for-phase-2-3-trials/)
  - Uganda's mRNA-1469 Phase Ib: approved 7 October, with no enrolment reported more than five weeks later.
  - ChAdOx1 Phase 1 in Oxford: launched 13 July, first dose 24 July (11 days).
- Historical comparison: in the 2018-2020 DRC Zaire outbreak, adding a second vaccine (J&J Ad26/MVA) took months after it was recommended. This is my general knowledge; I did not verify it in this session.
- Seasonality does not apply.

## 5. Other forecasts
- None of the collected Kalshi or Polymarket markets matches this question. The closest ones (Ebola countries, "Ebola pandemic") are unrelated.
- I found no Metaculus or Manifold market or expert forecast on candidate dosing in Tumaini.

## 6. Upcoming events before 27 November
- A DRC regulatory and ethics clearance announcement for one or both candidates, and a Tumaini protocol amendment.
- Shipment of ChAdOx1 BDBV and/or mRNA-1469 doses to Kinshasa or Bunia (mRNA-1469 needs cold-chain).
- WHO Disease Outbreak News (the last one was 6 November, so roughly weekly or biweekly updates are possible) and WHO Member State and press briefings.
- Possible announcements from Oxford, the Serum Institute, Moderna or CEPI. A first-dose press release is likely, since the first Ervebo dose got one.
- Doherty's "three to four weeks" window ends around 25 November to 2 December.
- Constraints: one site open as of 11 November, insecurity (more than 80 attacks on health facilities per Africa CDC), and a short 11-day window to the cutoff.

I found no public report that either ChAdOx1 BDBV or mRNA-1469 has been given to a Tumaini participant. As of 16 November 2026 the question stands at 0 of 2. Both candidates are still recommended "pending national approvals", and I could not find any report that the DRC regulator (ACOREP) has cleared either one.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-12 (last update): The EbolaIntel tracker says both candidates were recommended on 4 November for Tumaini "once national approvals are in place". The only Tumaini dosing it records is Ervebo, from 23 October. ChAdOx1 BDBV is listed in Phase 1 trials in Oxford (since 24 July) and Masaka, Uganda (since 6 October). mRNA-1469 is listed in a Phase 1 trial in Canada (since 3 August), plus a Uganda Phase Ib trial approved on 7 October with no enrolment reported. [EbolaIntel](https://ebolaintel.com/vaccines/investigational)
- ClinicalTrials.gov record NCT07842107 (read via its API) is stale: it was last updated 2026-10-05 and still shows "Not yet recruiting".
  - Design: one dose of a candidate Bundibugyo vaccine or a typhoid comparator on Day 1, then the other product on Day 29. Allocation is masked.
  - Each candidate enters through its own "vaccine-specific appendix", which means a protocol amendment.
  - Because allocation is masked, public reports might confirm that an arm is open without saying any individual was dosed with it. [CT.gov API](https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies/NCT07842107?fields=protocolSection.statusModule,protocolSection.armsInterventionsModule)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. No WHO, Moderna, Oxford, Serum Institute, CEPI, INRB or DRC Ministry of Health source I found reports a dose of either candidate in Tumaini.
- One conflicting claim: Wikipedia says that "as of 6 November, three candidate vaccines have been approved for inclusion", meaning Ervebo plus the two candidates. That probably refers to the WHO recommendation, not a national approval, and no other source backs it. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Ebola_epidemic)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-15: WHO Director-General Tedros said only that trials, "including the Tumaini trial and the development of new vaccine candidates, are advancing rapidly". He gave no dosing news. [Sahara Reporters](https://saharareporters.com/2026/11/15/who-confirms-over-11000-ebola-cases-5400-deaths-dr-congo-six-months-says-children-worst)
- 2026-11-14: K24 says both candidates "are not yet in Tumaini" and can enter only after national approvals. It reports four rings (WHO's figure on 11 November was 11), and vaccine results are expected in early 2027. [K24](https://k24.digital/lifestyle/health-and-fitness/kenya-to-launch-ksh4-7-billion-ebola-vaccine-trial-in-2027-as-drc-expands-tumaini-study)
- 2026-11-11: At the Member State briefing, WHO said "A trial using the Ervebo vaccine began last month" and that experts had recommended the two Bundibugyo-specific candidates. It gave no start date for them. [WHO](https://www.who.int/news-room/speeches/item/who-director-general-s-opening-remarks-at-the-member-state-briefing-on-ebola-outbreak-in-the-democratic-republic-of-the-congo---11-november-2026)
- 2026-11-10: Gavi says the candidates "will enter the trial following national approvals". [Gavi](https://www.gavi.org/vaccineswork/can-two-new-vaccines-help-turn-tide-against-ebola-caused-bundibugyo-virus)
- 2026-11-05: Coverage of Oxford says ChAdOx1 BDBV joins "subject to regulatory clearance", with no Tumaini start date. [Digital Journal](https://www.digitaljournal.com/article/oxford-vaccine-moves-towards-pivotal-trial-against-deadly-bundibugyo-ebola-virus/)
- 2026-11-04: Moderna's press release says mRNA-1469 will be evaluated in Tumaini "subject to regulatory approval". WHO's technical advisory group reviewed the evidence on 22 October. [BioSpace](https://www.biospace.com/press-releases/moderna-advances-investigational-bundibugyo-ebolavirus-vaccine-toward-phase-2-3-study)
- 2026-11-04: WHO announced the recommendation; the candidates enter "following national approvals". [WHO](https://www.who.int/news/item/04-11-2026-two-new-candidate-vaccines-to-join-ebola-trial-as-treatment-research-advances)

## 4. Base rates
- Within this outbreak, gaps between approval or launch and first dose have been:
  - Tumaini registered on ClinicalTrials.gov 2026-09-25; first Ervebo dose 23 October (some reports say 26 October), about 4 weeks later.
  - CEPI said on 13 October that the candidates were due to join; recommendation came 4 November; no dosing as of 16 November, which is at least 12 days and counting.
  - mRNA-1469 got Uganda ethics approval 7 October; no enrolment reported more than 5 weeks later.
  - The ChAdOx1 Uganda Phase 1 started 6 October, about 5 weeks after Oxford was dosing and about 4.5 months after the candidate was announced on 22 May.
- In the 2018-2020 North Kivu Zaire Ebola outbreak, the second vaccine (Ad26/MVA) took months after recommendation to be deployed in DRC, partly because of national regulatory and political delays. That date is from my own knowledge; I did not verify it in this search.
- Seasonality does not apply.

## 5. Other forecasts
- No Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or Metaculus market matches this question. The Kalshi markets supplied (Ebola countries, "Ebola pandemic" at 0.01) are not relevant.

## 6. Upcoming events before 27 November
- The main gate is ACOREP authorisation plus ethics approval of each candidate's appendix to the protocol. Neither has been reported.
- Next WHO Disease Outbreak News and situation updates, likely around 20 November; the last DON was 6 November.
- Possible next WHO Member State or media briefing, likely around 18-25 November.
- Possible announcements from CEPI, Oxford, the Serum Institute or Moderna about the "first participant dosed in Tumaini". Developers have announced every past first dose (Oxford, Canada, Uganda) within about 1-2 days.
- Logistics:
  - ChAdOx1 has stock: about 620,000 bulk doses, with about 3,000 investigational doses noted in trackers.
  - mRNA-1469 had about 12,000 vials that still needed filling, according to the advisory group's report, and it needs a cold chain in Bunia.
  - Only one Tumaini site was open as of 11 November.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) **Time left:** about 11 days, until 27 November 2026, 23:59 UTC.

(b) **Latest known value:** 0. The ebolaintel tracker (updated 12 November) and all WHO, Gavi, Moderna and K24 reports up to 16 November show no Tumaini dose of either ChAdOx1 BDBV or mRNA-1469. Both still need DRC national approval.

(c) **If nothing changed:** 0.

(d) **If the current trend continued:** WHO's Meg Doherty said dosing could start "within three to four weeks" of about 4-5 November. That puts the start around 25 November to 2 December, at or just after the cutoff. Such timelines usually slip. Several things would have to happen in about 11 days:
- DRC regulatory and ethics approval
- a protocol amendment
- shipment of doses
- site readiness, with only one site open
- a public report of the first dose

ChAdOx1 BDBV is the likelier first candidate because supply is stockpiled and the cold chain is simpler. mRNA-1469 is less likely because vials are unfilled, it needs a demanding cold chain, and its Uganda trial was approved on 7 October with no enrolment reported more than five weeks later. The trend outcome is most likely still 0.

(e) **Historical variation:** This is a step function. Earlier steps in this outbreak took several weeks:
- Ervebo arrived in Kinshasa on 21 August and the first Tumaini dose came about two months later.
- Adding a second vaccine in the 2018-2020 DRC outbreak took months after it was recommended.
- The fastest example, Oxford's Phase 1 trial, went from launch to first dose in 11 days, but in a far simpler setting.

(f) **Experts and markets:** No matching markets exist. The only expert signal is WHO's "3-4 weeks pending approval" estimate, which is borderline for the cutoff.

My estimates:
- ChAdOx1 BDBV dosed and reported by 27 November: about 15-18%
- mRNA-1469 dosed and reported by 27 November: about 5%
- Overall: P(0) ≈ 0.80, P(1) ≈ 0.16, P(2) ≈ 0.04

(g) **Unexpected scenarios:**
- **Low:** DRC approval or the protocol amendment stalls, insecurity in Ituri disrupts the single site, or a dose is given but not publicly reported until December. The result stays at 0.
- **High:** DRC grants fast-track approval for both candidates around 18-20 November, pre-positioned doses are given in a new ring, and WHO or Moderna announce the first doses within the week. The result is 2.

(c) If nothing changed: 0.

(d) If the current trend continued: Meg Doherty's "three to four weeks" estimate, given on 4-5 November, implies first doses around 25 November to 2 December. That window only just reaches the cutoff. Precedents in this outbreak point to slippage:
- Ervebo took about two months from arrival in Kinshasa to the first Tumaini dose.
- Uganda approved its mRNA-1469 Phase Ib on 7 October and had reported no enrolment more than five weeks later.

The trend therefore most likely gives 0. If anything happens, ChAdOx1 BDBV is the more likely candidate, because supply is ample and Phase 1 data already exist. mRNA-1469 faces fill-finish and cold-chain hurdles.

(e) Historical variation: none so far. This is a step change from 0 that requires several gates to clear within 11 days: DRC regulatory and ethics approval, a protocol amendment, shipment, dosing at a single open site, and a public report explicitly linked to Tumaini.

(f) Experts and markets: there are no matching markets. WHO's own estimate is optimistic and conditional on DRC approval. Gavi and K24 (10-14 November) still describe approval as pending. I estimate P(at least 1) at about 12-15% and P(2) at about 3%.

(g) Unexpected scenarios:
- Low: DRC approval is delayed, insecurity disrupts the Bunia site, or shipments are held up. The result is 0, which is already the base case.
- High: DRC fast-tracks approval of both candidates around 18-20 November, and pre-positioned ChAdOx1 doses plus some of the roughly 12,000 mRNA-1469 vials are given in rings by 25 November, with a WHO or MSF press release. That gives 1, or very unusually 2. The 99th percentile reflects that small chance of 2.
